_convention: Training compute = 6 * N_total * D (N_total = all parameters incl. tied embeddings, D = tokens processed). Sources and assumptions per model; ranges where the step count or packing is not published. Our own runs use the same 6*N*D convention in experiments/plot_published.py.

roneneldan/TinyStories-1M.assumption: steps not published; assumes the ~20 epochs the author states for 33M (20 x 476.2M GPT-Neo tokens)
roneneldan/TinyStories-1M.hardware: <= 30 h on one V100 (paper bound for all 1M-35M models)

roneneldan/TinyStories-3M.assumption: steps not published; assumes ~20 epochs as for 33M

roneneldan/TinyStories-8M.assumption: config: checkpoint-25750; 1,280 sequences/step as for 33M; low = one story per sequence, high = packed 512-token blocks

roneneldan/TinyStories-28M.assumption: config: checkpoint-21250; 1,280 sequences/step; unpacked vs packed

roneneldan/TinyStories-33M.assumption: author: 'about 20 epochs' (HF discussion #8); batch 80 x grad-accum 16 on 4x V100

stories260K.assumption: exact: iter_num 98,000 x 65,536 tokens/iter, read from the checkpoint config

_caveats: roneneldan models trained on all of TinyStories V1 train, which contains 30% of the V1 validation stories verbatim; llama2.c models trained on TinyStories_all_data shards that contain 68.6% of them. All scores here use only the 4,194 validation stories found in neither (experiments/clean_val_indices.json).

llama2.c models were trained on text with single-newline paragraph breaks; they are fed V1 text with '

' -> '
'. Bits per byte always use the original V1 byte count as the denominator, so every model is scored on the same information.
Published models are trained to convergence on many epochs (6-39). The comparison is quality reached per unit of training compute, not final quality.
